an3.80:4.2: Pali texts here read _aparagoyāna_, “west of Goyāna” (“cow-cart”), but no Goyāna is found elsewhere in this sense. The normal Sanskrit spelling is _aparagodānīya_, “bestowal of cows”, i.e. a land abundant in the wealth typified by cows. Now, _godānīya_ is a mere verbal variation of _godāvarī_, the name of the famed river that arises near Nashik, not far from modern Mumbai on the west coast ([snp5.1:2.3]()). Lands further west were reached by ship from that shore, and the river sometimes loaned its name to the place and people of Nashik. I propose we emend to “west of Godāvarī”.
an3.80:9.1: The lack of vocative in what follows indicates that this was not addressed to anyone, per Thai editions.
